title: Feasibility study of an online food and mood knowledge intervention to support health and wellbeing
official: An exploration of the Feasibility and Acceptability of an online food and Mood knowledge Intervention to Support Health and wellbeing (FAMISH)
summary:
Background and study aims
There has been substantial progress in reducing stigma and improving treatments for mental illness. However, the prevalence of common mental disorders, such as depression and anxiety, is not declining and may even be increasing. The individual and societal burden of poor mental health is substantial, and new treatment approaches are urgently required. 
Lifestyle modification, including dietary change, is a well-established intervention for metabolic disorders and other conditions. Despite this, nutrition and diet only began appearing in best practice guidance and United Kingdom (UK) government reports in 2005, and then largely in relation to physical health.
This lack of nutrition training contributes to the gap between evidence for lifestyle medicine and its integration into routine mental health care. Mental and substance use disorders remain the leading cause of disability worldwide, while poor diet is a major contributor to illness and early mortality.
Research from the Food & Mood Centre, which pioneered Nutritional Psychiatry, shows that diet and mental health are closely linked  and that dietary improvement can be both effective and cost-efficient in treating common mental disorders.

The aim of the study is to determine whether the well-established, 3-week, self-directed, freely-available "Food and Mood: Improving Mental Health Through Diet and Nutrition" online course (hereafter referred to as the FOC) is an acceptable and feasible dietary knowledge intervention for adults with a range of diagnosed mental illnesses accessing NHS mental health secondary care services.

Who can participate?
Participants will be NHS patients aged 16 years or older, living in England, and accessing mental health treatment services through Rotherham Doncaster and South Humber (RDaSH) NHS Foundation Trust. 

What does the study involve?
Patients will be invited to do an online course. The course will give them information about healthy eating that may help improve mental health and mood. The course is based on an existing programme designed by the Food and Mood Centre at Deakin University, Australia.
The course activities include reading some information and watching videos. The course offers you the chance to check your learning with some simple questions, but this is not recorded and just for your information.
Participants will complete a pre-course survey and a post-course survey.

Where is the study run from?
Rotherham Doncaster and South Humber NHS Foundation Trust (UK).

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
March 2026 to December 2027.

Who is funding the study?
Food and Mood Academy, Deaking University, Australia.

Who is the main contact?
Dr Kevin Williamson, kevin.williamson@nhs.net

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Are aged 16 years or older on the day of consent
2. Have sufficient capacity to provide informed consent
3. Can access the online course and surveys via a digital device (e.g., laptop, smartphone or tablet)
4. Are currently accessing mental health treatment via the study site NHS Mental Health Care Trust
Exclusion criteria:
1. Diagnosis of dementia
2. Disordered eating diagnosis
3. Have a special diet for a medical condition
4. Insufficient English language to be able to participate in the course
